newsitem.title: LEBANON: Active Beirut shares mixed on week.
newsitem.headline: Active Beirut shares mixed on week.

text.p: Most of the active stocks on the Beirut Stock Exchange were mixed in the week ended on Friday and dealers said Banque Audi was likely to touch a ceiling of $19.5 next week.
Banque Audi was steady on the week, while Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce rose, Solidere A and B fell and two industrial shares were mixed.
The BLOM stock index fell 0.91 percent to 902.87 and the LISPI share index rose 0.69 percent to 85.04. The LIBX bank index rose 1.37 to 120.10.
Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce rose to $14 from $13.625 on increased turnover of 27,348 shares. Last week's turnover was 19,284 shares.
"BLC was going up slowly throughout the week. Demand on the share has been developing. It was distributed on several price levels and its quantity was above recent weeks' average," a dealer said.
Audi held steady at $19.125. Turnover was 48,949 shares, down from last week's 71,348.
"There is still strong demand but on the $19.125 level. There is a perception that the share is approaching a ceiling. We are still expecting it to make the $19.5 next week," the dealer added.
The market is awaiting the imminent listing of a third bank, Bank of Beirut, whose $10 million private share placement prior to listing was 11 times oversubscribed at $110 million.
Listing of 30 percent of Bank of Beirut's shares is expected by mid-April.
Solidere A and B shares fell to $10.25 and $10.75 from $10.375 and $10.875 respectively on reduced turnover of 349,043 shares from 543,454 a week earlier.
Industrial pipemaker Eternit rose to $2 from $1.875 on sharply increased turnover of 19,760 from 7,250 last week.
Ciments Libanais was unchanged at $1.1875 on a turnover of 1,800 shares, down from 4,500. Two blocks of 25,000 shares each were traded on the floor at $1.25.
There was no trade in the two other listed firms: Uniceramic and Ciments Blancs.
Weekly BSE turnover fell to 496,900 from 645,836 and value was $5,048,627 against $7,277,705. Turnover included two blocks totalling 50,000 Ciments Libanais shares traded on the floor at $1.25.
